why: The statement asks whether any o-minimal theory has a trans-exponential function. No event exhibits one. Fu (2026) is the closest call: it proves o-minimality of R_an,exp,phi only under a regularity assumption that the paper itself calls necessary for o-minimality, and the record shows no phi verified to satisfy it. That is a reduction to an unproven condition, so it is none rather than case or whole; the 'Towards' title agrees. Padgett's work is a Hardy-field result with QE left open, and Miller's 2023 note is conditional on an antecedent believed false, so both are none. Krapp–Kuhlmann (ordered transexponential fields, no o-minimality) and the maximal Hardy fields paper settle different questions, so both are variant. Miller's 2026 talk only reports that the question is open. No AI system is credited in any event.
doubts: The record reports a Pfaffian-closure claim from Miller's notes, seen only in search excerpts: that the Pfaffian closure of R_exp is not exponentially bounded. If true, the question was answered yes before 2024. It contradicts Miller's own 2026 abstract, the Miller–Starchenko status note, Fu and the 2025 survey, and it was never opened, so it is not recorded as an event. Fu's paper was not read in full, so a verification of the regularity assumption for a specific phi in the unread part cannot be ruled out.
